evals.prompt: We should add dark mode to the settings page. Can you start on it?
evals.expected_output: The request is classified as a feature or behavior change. The reply routes to interview-me if the request is ambiguous, then names spec-driven-development and plan-work before any feature edit, and names the branch it will use. It writes no feature code, spec or task file.
expectations: The reply classifies the request as a feature or behavior change, not a docs-only change.
The reply names spec-driven-development and plan-work (or a task file) before any feature edit.
The reply names the branch it will use before the first feature edit.
The reply writes no feature code, spec or task file.

evals.prompt: The login test started failing after the last merge. I have no idea why. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The failure is routed to root-cause, not to a guessed fix. A branch is created before the first edit, and reproduction comes before any code change.
expectations: The reply routes to root-cause and asks for a reproduction before changing code.
The reply creates or names a branch before the first edit.
The reply does not claim a spec is needed for a single fix.
No fix is applied before the failure is reproduced.

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in the README: 'recieve' should be 'receive'.
evals.expected_output: The request is classified as docs-only. It is edited directly, and the git policy decides branch or direct; no spec or task file is created.
expectations: The reply classifies the request as docs-only.
The reply does not create a spec or a task file.
The reply uses docs/GIT.md to decide branch or direct.

evals.prompt: I have a hunch about onboarding but no shape yet. I think we should improve it. What next?
evals.expected_output: The request is classified as a hunch or vague idea. It routes to idea-refine before a spec, writes no spec/task/code, and names no branch before an artifact exists.
expectations: The reply classifies the request as a hunch or vague idea, not a ready feature.
The reply routes to idea-refine before spec-driven-development.
The reply writes no spec, task or code.
The reply does not start a branch before an artifact exists.

evals.prompt: Make the export flow work the usual way. You know what I mean.
evals.expected_output: The request has two readings, so it routes to interview-me. The reply asks one question and writes no spec or code.
expectations: The reply routes to interview-me because the request has more than one reading.
The reply writes no spec, task or code.
The reply does not implement or start a spec before the request has one reading.
